excerpts.text: Costco Wholesale Corporation and its subsidiaries (Costco or the Company) began operations in 1983, in Seattle, Washington. We are principally engaged in the operation of membership warehouses in the United States (U.S.) and Puerto Rico, Canada, Mexico, Japan, the United Kingdom (U.K.), Korea, Australia, Taiwan, China, Spain, France, Sweden, Iceland, and New Zealand. Costco operated 914, 890, and 861 warehouses worldwide at August 31, 2025, September 1, 2024, and September 3, 2023. The Company operates e-commerce sites in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Korea, Taiwan, Japan, and Australia. Our common stock trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market, under the symbol “COST.”

We report on a 52/53-week fiscal year, consisting of thirteen four-week periods and ending on the Sunday nearest the end of August. The first three quarters consist of three periods each, and the fourth quarter consists of four periods (five weeks in the thirteenth period in a 53-week year). The material seasonal impact in our operations is increased net sales and earnings during the winter holiday season. References to 2025 and 2024 relate to the 52-week fiscal years ended August 31, 2025, and September 1, 2024. References to 2023 relate to the 53-week fiscal year ended September 3, 2023.

We operate membership warehouses and e-commerce sites based on the concept that offering low prices on a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products in a wide range of categories will produce high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover. When combined with the operating efficiencies achieved by volume purchasing, efficient distribution and reduced handling of merchandise in no-frills, self-service warehouse facilities, these volumes and turnover enable us to operate profitably at significantly lower gross margins (net sales less merchandise costs) than most other retailers. We often sell inventory before we are required to pay for it, even while taking advantage of early payment discounts.

We buy most of our merchandise directly from suppliers and route it to cross-docking consolidation points (depots) or directly to our warehouses. Our depots receive large shipments from suppliers and quickly ship these goods to warehouses. This process creates freight volume and handling efficiencies, lowering costs associated with traditional multiple-step distribution channels. Our e-commerce operations ship merchandise through our depots and logistics operations, as well as through drop-ship and other delivery arrangements with our suppliers.

Our average warehouse space is approximately 147,000 square feet, with newer units being slightly larger. Floor plans are designed for efficiency in the use of selling space, the handling of merchandise, and the control of inventory. Because shoppers are attracted principally by the quality of merchandise and low prices, our warehouses are not elaborate. By strictly controlling the entrances and exits and using a membership format, we believe our inventory losses (shrinkage) are well below those of typical retail operations.

Our operating hours are shorter than many other retailers, and due to other efficiencies inherent in a warehouse club operation, we believe labor costs are lower relative to the volume of sales. In the U.S., we recently added exclusive shopping hours for our Executive members and our gasoline operations generally have extended hours. Merchandise is generally stored on racks above the sales floor and displayed on pallets containing large quantities, reducing labor required. In general, with variations by country, our warehouses accept certain credit cards, including Costco co-branded cards, debit cards, cash and checks, Executive member 2% reward certificates, co-brand cardholder rebates, and our proprietary stored-value card (shop card).

Our strategy is to provide our members with a broad range of high-quality merchandise at prices we believe are consistently lower than elsewhere. We seek to limit most items to fast-selling models, sizes, and colors. We carry less than 4,000 active stock keeping units (SKUs) per warehouse in our core warehouse business, significantly less than other broadline retailers. We average from 9,000 to 10,000 SKUs online, some of which are available in our warehouses. Many consumable products are offered for sale in case, carton, or multiple-pack quantities only. To promote member satisfaction, we generally accept returns of merchandise. On certain electronic items, we have a 90-day return policy and provide, free of charge, technical support services, as well as an extended warranty. Additional third-party warranty coverage is sold on certain electronic items and major appliances.

We offer merchandise and services in the following categories: (including sundries, dry grocery, candy, cooler, freezer, liquor, and tobacco) (including major appliances, small electronics, health and beauty aids, hardware, lawn and garden, sporting goods, tires, toys and seasonal, automotive, stamps, tickets, apparel, furniture, domestics, housewares, special order kiosk, and jewelry) (including meat, produce, deli, and bakery) (includes gasoline, pharmacy, optical, food court, hearing aids, and tire installation) (includes e-commerce, business centers, travel, and other) Warehouse ancillary operate primarily within, next to or near our warehouses, encouraging more frequent shopping. The number of warehouses with gas stations varies significantly by country. We operated 747 gas stations at the end of 2025. Our gasoline business represented approximately 10% of total net sales in 2025.

Our other businesses sell products and services that largely complement our warehouse operations. Our e-commerce operations give members convenience and a broader selection of goods and services. Net sales for e-commerce represented approximately 7% of total net sales in 2025. Digitally-enabled sales,

which represents sales delivered to members that are initiated through a digital device, whether fulfilled through a warehouse or distribution center, as well as Costco Travel, represented approximately 10% of total net sales in 2025. Our business centers carry items tailored for food services, convenience stores and offices and offer walk-in shopping and deliveries. Business centers are included in our total warehouse count. Costco Travel offers vacation packages, car rentals, cruises and other travel products exclusively for Costco members (offered to varying degrees in the U.S., Canada, Australia, and the U.K.).

We have direct relationships with many producers of brand-name merchandise. We do not obtain a significant portion of merchandise from any one supplier. When sources of supply become unavailable, we seek alternative sources or items. For future product supply need, we pursue diversification in our supply-chain and seek to expand in-country production. We also purchase and manufacture private-label merchandise, as long as quality and member demand are high and the value to our members is significant. Certain financial information for our segments and geographic areas is included in to the consolidated financial statements included in Item 8 of this Report.

Our members may utilize their memberships at all of our warehouses and e-commerce sites. Gold Star memberships are available to individuals; Business memberships are limited to businesses, including individuals with a business license or comparable document. Business members may add additional cardholders (affiliates), to which the same annual fee applies. Affiliates are not available for Gold Star members. Our annual fee for these memberships is $65 in the U.S. and varies in other countries. All paid memberships include a free household card.

Paid members (except affiliates) are eligible to upgrade to an Executive membership in the U.S., for an additional annual fee of $65. Executive memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,250 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses. The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.6% of worldwide net sales in 2025. Membership at the end of 2025, 2024, and 2023 was made up of the following (in thousands): Executive members represented 38,700, 35,400, and 32,300 of total paid members in 2025, 2024, and 2023.

We believe that our warehouses are among the most productive in the retail industry, owing largely to the commitment and efficiency of our employees. We seek to provide them not merely with employment but careers. Many attributes of our business contribute to the objective. The more significant include: competitive compensation and benefits; a commitment to employee development and promoting from within; and a target ratio of at least 50% of our base being full-time employees. These attributes contribute to what we consider, especially for the industry, a high retention rate. In 2025, in the U.S. and Canada that rate was approximately 94% for employees who have been with us for at least one year.

The commitment to “Take Care of Our Employees” includes promoting an inclusive and respectful workplace. We strive for an environment where all employees feel that they belong, are accepted, included, respected and supported. We demonstrate leadership commitment to inclusion through consistent communication, employee development and education, support of diversity and inclusion initiatives within the organization, community involvement, and supplier inclusion. Listening to our employees is one of the ways Costco takes care of its workforce. In 2025, we hosted the Costco Connects meetings, its second annual Costco Connects campaign. These open listening sessions are an invitation for employees to talk about what is on their minds and what is impacting them both personally and professionally. This allows Costco leaders to engage with their employees on a deeper level and for employees to build connections with each other. This year we had approximately 200,000 employees participate globally. Costco continues its efforts to develop future leaders, including through our supervisor in training (SIT) programs in the U.S. and Canada. In 2025, approximately 7,500 hourly employees completed the 6-week course.

thesis.text: Costco's membership-driven warehouse model continues to compound: revenue grew from $227.0B in FY2022 to $275.2B in FY2025 (8.2% YoY, 6.6% 3-yr CAGR), operating income rose from $7.8B to $10.4B, and net income from $5.8B to $8.1B, producing 27.8% ROE despite thin 3.8% operating and 2.9% net margins inherent to the model. Cash conversion is strong ($13.3B operating cash flow vs. $8.1B net income, $7.8B free cash flow) and the balance sheet is conservative (-$8.4B net debt, flat diluted shares at 444.8M), but two structural vulnerabilities deserve elevated weight rather than footnote status: (1) earnings quality is heavily concentrated in Executive members, who already drive approximately 73.6% of worldwide net sales and whose 2%-reward incentive structure ties future net sales and membership-fee growth to a single cohort's continued upgrade and spending behavior, and (2) the company's already-thin 3.8% operating margin leaves little room to absorb wage inflation or labor disruption given that compensation and benefits is explicitly its largest expense after merchandise cost across 341,000 employees (~5% unionized). Additional secondary risks include capex outpacing cash generation (capex from $3.9B to $5.5B against a 2.8% FCF margin), a working-capital-dependent model reliant on selling inventory before paying suppliers, softer international renewal rates (89.8% worldwide vs. 92.3% U.S./Canada) as the company expands into more of these markets (914 warehouses, up from 861), and a gasoline business (~10% of net sales) whose price volatility can distort reported revenue growth.
thesis.author: PM

bull.text: Top-line and profit growth remain robust: revenue grew from $227.0B (FY2022) to $275.2B (FY2025), 8.2% YoY and 6.6% 3-yr CAGR, while operating income rose from $7.8B to $10.4B and net income from $5.8B to $8.1B.
bull.author: PM

bull.text: Cash conversion is strong and the balance sheet is conservative: FY2025 operating cash flow of $13.3B exceeds net income of $8.1B, free cash flow was $7.8B, net debt is -$8.4B, and diluted shares are flat at 444.8M versus 444.8M in FY2022.
bull.author: PM

bull.text: The model converts thin margins into a high return on capital: despite 3.8% operating margin and 2.9% net margin in FY2025, ROE was 27.8%.
bull.author: PM

bull.text: Core membership economics still show healthy retention where the base is most mature: U.S./Canada renewal rate stood at 92.3% at end of FY2025, and Executive membership count grew from 32,300 thousand (2023) to 38,700 thousand (2025), evidencing continued upgrade demand.
bull.author: PM

bull.text: Ancillary and diversified revenue streams (gasoline ~10% of net sales, e-commerce ~7%, digitally-enabled/travel sales ~10%) and a diversified supplier base without reliance on any single supplier support resilience beyond the core warehouse format.
bull.author: PM

bear.text: Earnings quality is increasingly concentrated in a single, incentive-driven cohort: Executive members, who earn a 2% reward capped at $1,250/year, already account for approximately 73.6% of worldwide net sales, up from a base of 32,300 thousand to 38,700 thousand members, making both net sales and membership-fee income disproportionately exposed to any slowdown in this group's spending or renewal behavior.
bear.author: PM

bear.text: The operating margin buffer is thin relative to labor exposure: compensation and benefits is explicitly Costco's largest expense after merchandise cost, covering 341,000 employees (~5% unionized), while operating margin is only 3.8%, leaving little room to absorb wage inflation or labor disruption without material margin compression.
bear.author: PM

bear.text: Free cash flow generation is being outpaced by rising capital intensity: capex climbed from $3.9B (FY2022) to $5.5B (FY2025), and despite 8.2% revenue growth, FCF margin was just 2.8% ($7.8B FCF), indicating warehouse expansion is consuming a growing share of operating cash flow.
bear.author: PM

bear.text: The low-margin model is structurally dependent on favorable working-capital timing: Costco explicitly states it 'often sells inventory before we are required to pay for it, even while taking advantage of early payment discounts,' a dynamic that could be disrupted if supplier payment terms tighten or turnover slows.
bear.author: PM

bear.text: International renewal rates are meaningfully weaker than the U.S./Canada core (89.8% worldwide vs. 92.3% U.S./Canada), and as the company expands its international footprint (914 warehouses, up from 861 two years prior, across 14 countries/territories), this weaker cohort could pressure the blended renewal rate and membership-fee income further.
bear.author: PM

bear.text: Gasoline, a low-margin and price-volatile category, represented approximately 10% of total net sales in FY2025; swings in fuel prices could inflate or deflate the reported 8.2% YoY revenue growth without a proportional profit contribution, complicating assessment of core warehouse strength.
bear.author: PM

questions: What is the spending trajectory and per-capita net sales of Executive members versus non-Executive members over the last several years, and what would a plateau in Executive upgrade rates imply for both membership fee revenue and net sales growth?
How does comparable/core merchandise sales growth look when gasoline and other commodity-price-sensitive categories are stripped out of the 8.2% YoY revenue growth figure?
What are the terms and timing of major union contracts, and what wage escalation assumptions are embedded in near-term labor cost planning given the 3.8% operating margin?
What is the renewal rate trend by individual country or region (rather than just the worldwide 89.8% blended figure), and which specific international markets are dragging it down?
What returns (e.g., payback period, warehouse-level sales ramp) is Costco generating on the incremental capex used for international expansion, particularly in markets with weaker renewal rates?
How have days payable outstanding and supplier payment terms trended recently, and is there any indication that early payment discount economics or supplier terms are tightening?
What percentage of total capex is allocated to new warehouse openings versus maintenance/remodels, and how does that mix affect the FCF margin trajectory going forward?

verdict_rationale.text: The core financial trends—revenue growth from $227.0B to $275.2B, operating income from $7.8B to $10.4B, strong cash conversion ($13.3B operating cash flow vs. $8.1B net income), and a conservative balance sheet (-$8.4B net debt)—remain intact and support the compounding thesis. However, the red team surfaced two high-severity, thesis-relevant risks that were previously understated: extreme earnings concentration in the Executive member cohort (73.6% of worldwide net sales) and a labor cost structure that is Costco's largest expense against an already-thin 3.8% operating margin. Neither objection breaks the thesis, but both materially affect the risk/reward calculus and warrant further quantitative diligence (e.g., Executive spend elasticity, union contract exposure, capex returns in weaker-renewal international markets) before forming a firm view.
verdict_rationale.author: PM

analyst_claims.text: Costco's business model centers on membership warehouse retail, selling a limited assortment (less than 4,000 active SKUs per warehouse) of nationally-branded and private-label merchandise across 914 warehouses in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, U.K., Korea, Australia, Taiwan, China, Spain, France, Sweden, Iceland, and New Zealand as of fiscal 2025, up from 890 and 861 in the prior two years.
analyst_claims.author: Business analyst

analyst_claims.text: The company's low-margin, high-volume model is enabled by rapid inventory turnover and operating efficiencies (cross-docking depots, no-frills warehouses, lower labor costs), allowing it to operate profitably at gross margins significantly lower than most retailers even as revenue grew from $227.0B in FY2022 to $275.2B in FY2025.
analyst_claims.author: Business analyst

analyst_claims.text: Membership fees are a key profit driver and demonstrate customer stickiness: annual fees are $65 in the U.S., Executive members (who pay an additional $65 and earn 2% rewards) grew to 38,700 thousand members in 2025 from 32,300 thousand in 2023 and now represent approximately 73.6% of worldwide net sales, while worldwide renewal rate stood at 89.8% (92.3% in U.S./Canada) at end of 2025.
analyst_claims.author: Business analyst

analyst_claims.text: Ancillary businesses—gasoline (approximately 10% of total net sales in 2025, operated through 747 gas stations), e-commerce (approximately 7% of net sales), and digitally-enabled sales including Costco Travel (approximately 10% of net sales)—complement the core warehouse model and drive incremental traffic and revenue diversification.
analyst_claims.author: Business analyst

analyst_claims.text: Despite thin margins inherent to the warehouse model (operating margin 3.8% and net margin 2.9% in FY2025), Costco converts sales into strong returns, with return on equity of 27.8% in FY2025, supported by operating income growing from $7.8B in FY2022 to $10.4B in FY2025.
analyst_claims.author: Business analyst

analyst_claims.text: The company maintains a diversified supplier base with direct relationships with many brand-name producers, stating it does not obtain a significant portion of merchandise from any one supplier, and pursues supply-chain diversification and in-country production to mitigate supply risk.
analyst_claims.author: Business analyst

analyst_claims.text: Costco's balance sheet reflects disciplined capital allocation with rising capital expenditures ($3.9B in FY2022 to $5.5B in FY2025) funding continued warehouse expansion, while maintaining a net cash position of -$8.4B (net debt) at FY2025 and growing free cash flow to $7.8B.
analyst_claims.author: Business analyst

analyst_claims.text: Revenue grew from $227.0B in FY2022 to $275.2B in FY2025, with the most recent year showing 8.2% YoY growth and a 6.6% three-year CAGR, indicating steady top-line expansion.
analyst_claims.author: Financial analyst

analyst_claims.text: Operating margin remains thin at 3.8% in FY2025, though operating income rose from $7.8B in FY2022 to $10.4B in FY2025, showing margin stability alongside absolute profit growth.
analyst_claims.author: Financial analyst

analyst_claims.text: Net income increased from $5.8B in FY2022 to $8.1B in FY2025, with net margin at 2.9% in FY2025, consistent with a low-margin, high-volume business model.
analyst_claims.author: Financial analyst

analyst_claims.text: Cash conversion is strong: operating cash flow of $13.3B in FY2025 exceeds net income of $8.1B, and free cash flow was $7.8B (2.8% FCF margin) after capital expenditures of $5.5B.
analyst_claims.author: Financial analyst

analyst_claims.text: Capital intensity has risen, with capital expenditures increasing from $3.9B in FY2022 to $5.5B in FY2025, tracking the company's revenue growth.
analyst_claims.author: Financial analyst

analyst_claims.text: The balance sheet is conservatively levered, with long-term debt of $5.7B in FY2025 against cash of $14.2B, producing negative net debt of -$8.4B and a return on equity of 27.8%.
analyst_claims.author: Financial analyst

analyst_claims.text: Shareholder dilution is negligible, with diluted shares essentially flat at 444.8M in FY2025 versus 444.8M in FY2022, a 0.0% YoY change.
analyst_claims.author: Financial analyst

analyst_claims.text: Costco's business model is built on operating profitably at 'significantly lower gross margins than most other retailers,' which leaves thin structural buffers: operating margin was 3.8% and net margin only 2.9% in FY2025, so any cost inflation, tariff pass-through, or pricing pressure could disproportionately compress earnings.
analyst_claims.author: Risk analyst

analyst_claims.text: Free cash flow generation is being outpaced by rising capital intensity: capital expenditures climbed from $3.9B in FY2022 to $5.5B in FY2025, and despite 8.2% revenue growth in FY2025, free cash flow margin was just 2.8% ($7.8B FCF), indicating expansion is consuming a growing share of operating cash flow.
analyst_claims.author: Risk analyst

analyst_claims.text: Gasoline sales represented approximately 10% of total net sales in FY2025, a low-margin, price-volatile category; large swings in fuel prices or demand could create outsized swings in reported revenue growth without a commensurate profit impact, complicating trend analysis.
analyst_claims.author: Risk analyst

analyst_claims.text: Profitability is increasingly concentrated in a single membership tier: Executive members, who earn a 2% reward capped at $1,250/year, accounted for approximately 73.6% of worldwide net sales in FY2025, up from prior periods (Executive member count grew from 32,300 thousand in 2023 to 38,700 thousand in 2025), making earnings sensitive to any slowdown in this cohort's spending or renewal behavior.
analyst_claims.author: Risk analyst

analyst_claims.text: Membership renewal, a key recurring-revenue driver, is not universal: renewal rates were 92.3% in the U.S./Canada and only 89.8% worldwide at the end of FY2025, meaning international markets show a meaningfully weaker retention profile that could pressure membership fee income if it deteriorates further.
analyst_claims.author: Risk analyst

analyst_claims.text: The company explicitly relies on selling inventory before having to pay suppliers, 'even while taking advantage of early payment discounts' — a working-capital-dependent model that could be disrupted if supplier payment terms tighten or inventory turnover slows.
analyst_claims.author: Risk analyst

analyst_claims.text: Compensation and benefits is Costco's largest expense after merchandise cost, covering 341,000 employees worldwide with roughly 5% unionized; given the company's already-thin operating margin (3.8% in FY2025), sustained wage inflation or labor disruption represents a disproportionate risk to profitability.
analyst_claims.author: Risk analyst

objections.text: The thesis frames rising capex as supporting reinvestment, but capex growth is outpacing the cash-generation benefit: even with 8.2% revenue growth, FCF margin was only 2.8% ($7.8B FCF) after capex rose from $3.9B to $5.5B, meaning warehouse expansion is consuming an increasing share of operating cash flow rather than simply funding growth from a position of comfort.
objections.author: Red team

objections.text: The model's structural fragility goes beyond thin margins: Costco explicitly states it 'often sells inventory before we are required to pay for it, even while taking advantage of early payment discounts,' meaning the low-margin business depends on favorable working-capital timing with suppliers that could be disrupted if payment terms tighten.
objections.author: Red team

objections.text: Earnings quality concentration in Executive members is more acute than a simple growth story: Executive members earn a 2% reward capped at $1,250/year and already represent approximately 73.6% of worldwide net sales, so a plateau or slowdown in this specific, reward-incentivized cohort (which grew from 32,300K to 38,700K members) would disproportionately impact both membership fee income and net sales growth simultaneously.
objections.author: Red team

objections.text: As Costco continues international expansion (914 warehouses across 14 countries/territories, up from 861 two years prior), the weaker 89.8% worldwide renewal rate versus 92.3% U.S./Canada suggests newer international markets renew less reliably, which could pressure the blended renewal rate further as international mix grows.
objections.author: Red team

objections.text: Gasoline, a low-margin and price-volatile category, represented approximately 10% of total net sales in 2025; large swings in fuel prices could inflate or deflate the reported 8.2% YoY revenue growth without a proportional profit contribution, meaning the top-line growth rate cited in the thesis may partly reflect commodity price movements rather than core warehouse strength.
objections.author: Red team

objections.text: The thesis acknowledges labor risk but understates its bite: compensation and benefits is explicitly Costco's largest expense after merchandise cost, covering 341,000 employees with about 5% unionized, against an operating margin of only 3.8% in FY2025 — leaving little room to absorb wage inflation or labor disruption without material margin compression.
objections.author: Red team
